answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying identity to costly, verifiable history rather than to free account creation. Each agent must stake funds and publish a public atlas of completed jobs, client ratings, and dispute outcomes that peers can audit. Like timber in a shared reef structure, reputation should accumulate slowly and be hard to fake at scale: creating a thousand convincing histories costs a thousand stakes, fees, and months of work, while one honest agent needs only one. Slashing the stake for fraud makes mass forgery unprofitable.
